lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Galatians: overview
nodes.d: Paul writes to the churches of Galatia, who were turning to another gospel, to defend justification by faith, the freedom of the sons of God and life by the Spirit (1:1-6:18).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul wrote to the Galatians and what he says the true gospel is?
ev: Say what problem prompted the letter (1:6-9)
Name the three parts: Paul's defence (1-2), justification by faith (3-4), living by the Spirit (5-6)

nodes.t: There is only one gospel
nodes.d: Paul greets the Galatians, is amazed that they are turning to another gospel, and pronounces a curse on anyone, even an angel, who preaches a different gospel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says there is no other gospel, using Galatians 1:6-9?
ev: Say what Christ gave himself for (1:4)
State what Paul says of anyone who preaches another gospel (1:8-9)

nodes.t: Paul's gospel and call by revelation
nodes.d: Paul says he received the gospel by the revelation of Jesus Christ, not from men, and tells of his former persecution of the church, God's call, his time in Arabia and his first visit to Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Paul says he came to preach the gospel, using Galatians 1:11-24?
ev: Say how Paul received his gospel (1:11-12)
Describe what Paul was like before his call (1:13-14)
Say what the churches of Judaea said about him (1:23-24)

nodes.t: Paul and the apostles at Jerusalem
nodes.d: Fourteen years later Paul went to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus, refused to give in to false brothers who wanted Titus circumcised, and was given the right hand of fellowship by James, Cephas and John.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened at Jerusalem in Galatians 2:1-10 and why Paul would not give way?
ev: Say why Titus was not circumcised (2:3-5)
Describe the agreement about preaching to the Gentiles and the circumcised (2:7-9)
Name what they asked Paul to remember (2:10)

nodes.t: Paul opposes Peter at Antioch
nodes.d: Paul tells how he opposed Peter to his face at Antioch for withdrawing from eating with Gentiles out of fear, since this was not in step with the truth of the gospel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul confronted Peter, using Galatians 2:11-14?
ev: Describe what Peter did and why (2:12)
Say why Paul rebuked him (2:14)

nodes.t: Justified by faith in Christ, crucified with Christ
nodes.d: Paul says a person is not justified by works of the law but by faith in Jesus Christ, and that he has been crucified with Christ and now lives by faith in the Son of God who loved him and gave himself for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says a person is justified, using Galatians 2:16 and 2:20?
ev: Quote the main claim of 2:16
Explain what Paul means by being crucified with Christ (2:20)
Say what would follow if righteousness came by the law (2:21)

nodes.t: Received the Spirit by hearing with faith
nodes.d: Paul asks the foolish Galatians whether they received the Spirit and saw miracles by works of the law or by hearing with faith, since they began in the Spirit.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul argues from the Galatians' own experience of the Spirit in Galatians 3:1-5?
ev: Say what question Paul asks in 3:2
Explain why he calls the Galatians foolish (3:1, 3:3)

nodes.t: Abraham, faith and the blessing for the nations
nodes.d: Paul argues that Abraham believed God and it was counted to him for righteousness, so those of faith are Abraham's children, and that Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law so that the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Galatians 3:6-9 connects Abraham's faith to the Gentiles?
ev: Quote what Paul says Abraham did (3:6)
Explain who are the children of Abraham (3:7)
Say what the scripture foresaw (3:8)
Explain how Christ redeemed us from the curse (3:13-14)

nodes.t: The promise and the law
nodes.d: Paul argues that the promise to Abraham and his seed, who is Christ, cannot be cancelled by the law that came 430 years later, and that the law was added because of transgressions until the seed should come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says the law relates to the promise made to Abraham in Galatians 3:15-22?
ev: Explain why the law does not cancel the promise (3:15-18)
Say who the seed is (3:16)
Say why the law was added (3:19)
Say what the scripture has concluded about all (3:22)

nodes.t: Sons of God in Christ: neither Jew nor Greek
nodes.d: Paul says the law was a schoolmaster to bring us to Christ, that all who are baptized into Christ and have faith are children of God, one in Christ, and Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how someone becomes a child of God and heir of the promise, using Galatians 3:26-29?
ev: Explain the picture of the schoolmaster (3:24-25)
List the distinctions Paul says are gone in Christ (3:28)
Say what believers are in Christ (3:29)

nodes.t: Redeemed to be sons and heirs
nodes.d: Paul compares the heir under guardians to people under the elements of the world, and says that when the time was full God sent his Son under the law to redeem those under the law so that we receive adoption, and God sent the Spirit of his Son crying Abba, Father.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God did "in the fulness of time" and what it means to be a son, using Galatians 4:4-7?
ev: Describe the heir who is still a child (4:1-2)
Say what God did when the fulness of time came (4:4-5)
Say what the Spirit cries (4:6)

nodes.t: Paul's plea: do not turn back
nodes.d: Paul asks why the Galatians, now known by God, are turning back to weak and beggarly elements and observing days and seasons, recalls their warmth toward him, and pleads with them as a mother in labour until Christ is formed in them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Paul's pleading with the Galatians in Galatians 4:8-20?
ev: Say what Paul fears (4:11)
Describe how the Galatians first received Paul (4:13-15)
Say what Paul wants formed in them (4:19)

nodes.t: Two sons, two covenants: Hagar and Sarah
nodes.d: Paul uses Abraham's two sons, one by the bondwoman and one by the free woman, as an allegory of two covenants, and says believers are children of promise like Isaac and not children of the bondwoman.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul reads the story of Hagar and Sarah in Galatians 4:21-31?
ev: Say who the two sons and their mothers are (4:22-23)
Explain the two covenants named in 4:24-26
Say who Paul says we are like (4:28, 4:31)
Quote the scripture Paul cites in 4:30

nodes.t: Stand fast in the liberty of Christ
nodes.d: Paul tells the Galatians to stand fast in the liberty with which Christ has made them free, warns that anyone who accepts circumcision as a way to be justified falls from grace, and says what counts is faith working through love.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says Christ is of no effect to those who seek justification by the law (Galatians 5:4)?
ev: Say what Paul warns happens if they are circumcised (5:2-4)
Say what avails in Christ Jesus (5:6)
Explain the picture of leaven (5:9)

nodes.t: Walking by the Spirit: works of the flesh and fruit of the Spirit
nodes.d: Paul says freedom is for serving one another in love, that the whole law is fulfilled in loving your neighbour, and contrasts the works of the flesh with the fruit of the Spirit for those who walk in the Spirit.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the fruit of the Spirit from Galatians 5:22-23 and explain the difference between flesh and Spirit?
ev: Say how liberty is to be used (5:13)
List some works of the flesh (5:19-21) and the fruit of the Spirit (5:22-23)
Say what belongs to those who are Christ's (5:24)

nodes.t: Bearing burdens, sowing and reaping
nodes.d: Paul teaches restoring a person overtaken in a fault gently, bearing one another's burdens, and sowing to the Spirit rather than to the flesh, and not growing weary in doing good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul means by "whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap" in Galatians 6:7-9?
ev: Say how to restore someone who has fallen (6:1)
Explain the sowing and reaping principle (6:7-8)
Say who we should do good to (6:10)

nodes.t: Boasting only in the cross
nodes.d: Paul closes in his own hand, says those who press circumcision want to avoid persecution for the cross, that he glories only in the cross of Christ, and that what counts is a new creature, and he bears the marks of Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul glories only in the cross of Christ (Galatians 6:14)?
ev: Say what Paul glories in (6:14)
Say what counts instead of circumcision or uncircumcision (6:15)

nodes.t: Genesis: overview
nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.t: God calls Abram
nodes.d: God calls Abram to leave his country and promises to make him a great nation and bless all the families of the earth through him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what God promised Abram in Genesis 12:1-3?
ev: State the promises of 12:1-3
Say that Abram went as the LORD told him

nodes.t: God's covenant with Abram
nodes.d: God confirms his promise of offspring and land to Abram and makes a covenant with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God promised Abram in Genesis 15 and how Abram responded?
ev: Describe the promises of offspring and land
Read 15:6 and say what Abram believed

nodes.t: Abram believed and it was counted as righteousness
nodes.d: Genesis 15:6 records that Abram believed the LORD and it was counted to him as righteousness, the verse Paul explains in Romans 4.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Genesis 15:6 in their own words?
ev: Quote or paraphrase 15:6 accurately
Say who or what Abram believed

nodes.t: Isaac is born
nodes.d: God keeps his promise: Sarah bears Isaac to Abraham in his old age.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Isaac was born?
ev: Retell how God kept his promise

nodes.t: Hagar and the birth of Ishmael
nodes.d: Sarai, still childless, gives her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abram; Hagar conceives and is treated harshly and flees. The angel of the LORD finds her at a spring, tells her to return, promises many descendants and names her son Ishmael, and she calls God the one who sees her.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened to Hagar in the wilderness and what she learned about God?
ev: Explain how Hagar came to be Abram's wife (16:1-3)
Tell what the angel of the LORD says to Hagar and what she calls the LORD (16:7-13)

nodes.t: Hagar and Ishmael are sent away
nodes.d: After Isaac is weaned, Sarah sees Ishmael mocking and asks that he and Hagar be cast out. God tells Abraham that his seed will be called in Isaac but he will also make a nation of Ishmael; in the wilderness God hears the boy's voice and opens Hagar's eyes to a well.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God promised about Ishmael, even as Isaac was the child of promise?
ev: Say what God told Abraham in 21:12-13
Describe how God provided for Hagar and Ishmael in the wilderness (21:17-20)

nodes.t: Leviticus: overview
nodes.d: Leviticus gives the LORD's instructions from the tabernacle: the offerings, the consecration of the priests, clean and unclean, the day of atonement, holy living, the feasts, the jubilee, and the blessings and curses of obedience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a one-sentence summary of what Leviticus is about?
ev: Name the main sections of Leviticus (offerings, priests, clean and unclean, atonement, holiness, feasts, jubilee, blessings and curses).

nodes.t: Not like Egypt or Canaan: sexual boundaries
nodes.d: Leviticus 18 calls Israel not to follow the practices of Egypt or Canaan, listing forbidden sexual relations, Molech worship and other practices, and warns that the land vomits out nations that defile it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the chapter says the LORD is giving these commands, using what verses 3 and 24-30 say?
ev: Say whose ways Israel is told not to follow (18:3).
State the consequence the chapter gives for defiling the land (18:24-28).
Find 18:5 and say what it promises to the person who does the LORD's statutes.

nodes.t: "Ye shall be holy": laws for neighbours
nodes.d: Leviticus 19 gathers commands under the call to be holy because the LORD is holy: honouring parents, sabbaths, leaving gleanings for the poor, honest dealing, no partiality, loving one's neighbour as oneself, care for the stranger and just weights.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list some ways Leviticus 19 says holiness shows up in daily life?
ev: Name at least five commands from the chapter that deal with how to treat other people.
Find the command to love the neighbour (19:18) and the command about the stranger (19:33-34).

nodes.t: Deuteronomy: overview
nodes.d: Deuteronomy records Moses' words to Israel on the plains of Moab in the fortieth year: a review of the journey, the ten commandments and the call to love the LORD, the laws for life in the land, the covenant renewal with its blessings and curses, Moses' song and blessing, and his death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain where Israel is and what Moses is doing throughout Deuteronomy?
ev: Describe Deuteronomy as Moses' speeches before Israel enters the land and name its main parts.

nodes.t: Laws for the family
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 21:10-23 gives rules about a captive woman taken as a wife, the firstborn right of the son of an unloved wife, the stubborn and rebellious son brought to the elders, and the burial before nightfall of a man hanged on a tree, who is accursed of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the rule about the firstborn of an unloved wife and the rule for a hanged man?
ev: Name the four situations in this section.
Say when a hanged man's body was to be buried and why (21:22-23).

nodes.t: Stones, altar and the curses from Ebal
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 27 commands that on crossing the Jordan Israel set up stones with the law written on them and an altar on mount Ebal, and that tribes stand on Gerizim to bless and Ebal to curse, with Levites declaring twelve curses to each of which all the people say Amen.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Israel was to do at Gerizim and Ebal?
ev: Say which tribes stood on which mount.
Name several of the sins cursed and what the people answer (27:15-26).

nodes.t: Sing, barren one: the covenant of peace
nodes.d: The barren woman is told to sing and enlarge her tent, the LORD her husband has called her back with mercy, swears as with the waters of Noah, and promises a covenant of peace that will not be removed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD compares his promise in Isaiah 54:9-10 to the waters of Noah?
ev: Describe the call to the barren woman (54:1-3)
Say what the LORD compares his oath to (54:9)
Quote the promise in 54:10

nodes.t: Habakkuk: overview
nodes.d: The burden Habakkuk saw: his complaints about violence in Judah and the LORD's answers, the vision to wait for in which the just live by faith, woes on the proud, and a prayer ending in rejoicing in the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Habakkuk moves from complaint to rejoicing?
ev: Describe the pattern of complaint and answer in chapters 1-2
Say how the book ends (3:17-19)

nodes.t: The vision to wait for; the just live by faith
nodes.d: Habakkuk stands on his watch; the LORD tells him to write the vision, which will surely come though it tarries, and contrasts the proud, whose soul is not upright, with the just, who shall live by his faith.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the contrast of Habakkuk 2:4 and say what the LORD tells Habakkuk to do with the vision?
ev: Say what Habakkuk does and what the LORD tells him to do (2:1-3)
Read 2:4 and state the contrast
Find where Paul cites it (Romans 1:17)
